newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds ready for fresh push up after restful break.
newsitem.headline: Bunds ready for fresh push up after restful break.

text.p: German Bund futures on Thursday tracked back down to fill the gap left behind in their spirited rally on Wednesday and now look set up for a fresh push higher.

After leaping to contract highs on Wednesday, inspired by firmer U.S. markets, the German market needed some consolidation in this session. Now, the trend is intact and will continue to drive prices higher, analysts said.
"At the moment we have to stick with the trend," said David Sneddon, vice president of fixed income at CSFB in London. "There is no point trying to pick tops in this market."
By 1414 GMT, the DTB September Bund future was trading 10 basis points higher on the day at 103.35, having been to a low of 103.09 and a high of 103.47 so far this session.
Analysts said the main longer-term target on the upside was at 104.04 -- the all-time high for Bund futures -- but said the market may see a few more ups and down before then.
Analysts at MMS international said convincing break to hold above 103.35 was needed before investors could get excited again about upside potential.
But as long as support in the 102.90 to 102.70 region did not come under pressure the outlook would remain bullish.

CSFB's Sneddon agreed: "The market has been down, filled the gap, tested it, and bounced back up," he said. "Only if we start to come back below 102.90 would I suspect that some kind of more lengthy correction was on its way."

Analysts noted severe curve-flattening in both cash and futures markets in the past few sessions, saying there was some potential that traders would begin to put on steepening trades in the coming days to benefit from any correction in this move.
Some said that with the shorter-dated cash paper and futures contracts under pressure, gains at the long end might also be limited until short prices recovered.
The mark, which had reached a low of 1.84 against the dollar in earlier business, was trading at 183.26 by 1440 GMT.
